\[
x \leftarrow \frac{1}{\lvert W(x) \rvert} \sum_{y \in W(x)} y,
\qquad
W(x) = \{y : \lvert y_s - x_s \rvert \le h_s,\ \lVert y_c - x_c \rVert \le h_c\}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(x_s, x_c\): The position and the color of a point
- \(h_s, h_c\): The spatial and color radii
- \(W(x)\): The window around x

Each pixel is a point x in a joint space of position x_s and color x_c. The window W(x) holds the pixels within the spatial radius h_s and the color radius h_c. Mean shift moves x to the mean of its window and repeats. The mean always points uphill on the density of the points, so x climbs to a peak, a mode, as Comaniciu and Meer showed. OpenCV stops after 5 steps or when the shift falls below 1, and gives the pixel the color where it stopped. Pixels in one object climb to the same mode, so they get nearly the same color. Edges stay sharp, because a pixel across an edge is outside the color radius. The regions are then the connected patches of similar color.
